text:
julia: heads up — noticed a p99 jump in ap-south H100 canary after merge 4231, looks like kernel selector chose slower path for many sequences :eyes:

sanjay: saw that too, p50 fine but p99 up ~120ms. CI perf job failed on the same commit (ci-bot posted failure).

ci-bot: perf-ci: ap-south/h100/serving_runtime_regression — threshold exceeded (p99 240ms -> 360ms) https://ci.internal.redwood/jobs/9082 :warning:

ana: posting a quick flamegraph from the failing CI run:
```
flamegraph.svg (attached)
hot stack: kernel_selector::score_kernels -> kernel_io_path -> alloc_kv_page
percent CPU: kernel_selector 34%, kv_cache 22%
```

mike: hmm kernel_selector spike + kv_cache allocs. any chance batching heuristics changed? PR 4231 touched prefill/batch-sampler.

julia: yes 4231 modified small-batch fallback; it intentionally avoids coalescing sequences <8 tokens to reduce latency. but looks like on H100 ap-south workload many short+long mixes cause selector to pick a generic kernel with worse headroom.

sanjay: started git bisect locally, reproduces on ap-south emu. bisect points at commit 7f3d2b (PR 4231) -> reverting that commit in canary brings p99 back down.

mike: can you paste the reproduction command?

sanjay: repro script I used:
```bash
# run perf harness with mix profile
./tools/bench_serving --region ap-south --hw h100 --profile mixed-short-long --concurrency 48 --duration 600
```
output snippet:
```
QPS 120 rps
p50 22ms p95 110ms p99 360ms
CPU: kernel_selector spike
```

ana: I profiled the kernel selection path with sampling: the selector now favors the generic kernel when the batch has both short & long sequences because the batching heuristic reports high variance. The generic kernel avoids tail-optimized attention which is faster for long-only batches but is ~1.4x slower for the short prefix case we have.

julia: that maps to KV spill events: small short sequences cause frequent kv-cache lookups and occasional page fault-like allocations when the prefill path excites a prefill-evict race. KV allocator logs show repeated evict->alloc cycles.

mike: so two interacting factors: new batching heuristic marks the batch as mixed -> selector picks generic kernel -> combined with kv churn -> large p99. annoying.

julia: agree. immediate mitigation options: 1) hold canary/rollout for all ap-south H100 fleets (deploy-bot hold) 2) revert PR 4231 to restore previous heuristic 3) patch selector to bias toward short-first kernel when kv-churn metric high 4) add an integration perf gate in CI with mixed-short-long profile.

deploy-bot: rollout status: canary in ap-south/h100 currently at 30%. hold requested by julia. pausing further rollout. :pause_button:

mike: I vote revert first, quick and safe. then follow-up patch that instruments kv-churn into selection.

ana: will draft a selector patch that checks KV_CHURN_RATE and batch_variance, but it needs unit tests + perf CI.

sanjay: pushing a revert PR now (revert: PR 4231) and triggering an emergency canary rollback test. Will post CI links.

sanjay: ci-bot shows rollback test in progress: https://ci.internal.redwood/jobs/9090 :hourglass_flowing_sand:

julia: thanks. after rollback we should run the mixed profile perf job as a gating test on PRs touching batching/kernel selector. adding to checklist.

mike: also file an SLO ticket to track this class of regressions; maybe add synthetic that simulates interleaved short/long sequences.

julia: created ticket RW-OPS-1192 and assigned to eng-runtime. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: rollback test passed in ap-south/h100 canary — p99 back to baseline. https://ci.internal.redwood/jobs/9090/result :white_check_mark:

mike: great. followups: ana to prototype selector change, sanjay to add perf gate, julia to post postmortem and lessons for rollout policies.

ana: will post a short RFC with microbench numbers for selector bias and KV_CHURN threshold.

julia: closing the thread once RFC linked here. thanks all. :sparkles:
